readiness_evidence: Not ready to offer. No verified harness has run the delegated calendar route, so no replay rollout is recorded and Grok Bot and Base44 Superagent keep their current recommended releases. Grok Bot's documented replay still expects no calendar event. The Muse session recorded below is an unverified-harness run, and it did not do the required restart after the slot was chosen, so this release stays deferred.

Not a Base44 Superagent fix: the 0.10.2 Base44 Superagent replay already connected Google Calendar with a token and posted the raw event link, so that harness keeps the connector route. The target is a harness whose platform can write calendar events itself but cannot hand a token to the CLI.

Offline: `calendar connect --mode events --route delegated` completes the gate without a token and is refused for free/busy; availability on that route is marked as not checked against the user's calendar; a late connect at the summary keeps the chosen time; a saved delegated choice is reused without a token and is never treated as an expired one. After payment the booked message comes first, then one create request with a one-time request id; `calendar record-event` records only a report whose times match the booking (any offset), refuses incomplete, repeated, or unknown reports, and a failed report tells the user to add the event themselves. Move, cancel, and bulk cleanup hand the same kind of request to the platform, `flow status` re-issues an unreported one, and an event keeps the route it was written on. Connector and local OAuth behave as before. The full suite passes.

Offline: `calendar connect --mode events --route delegated --delegated-can-read-busy` opts into a second kind of request for a platform that can read Google Calendar busy times itself but still cannot hand the CLI a token. `flow availability` then asks for busy intervals over its exact search window before showing any time (`calendar_delegated_busy_request`), `calendar report-busy --request-id <id> --busy START,END` (repeatable) or `--none` records them once, and the next `flow availability` for that same window filters the returned slots and marks the calendar checked. A stale or unknown request id is refused; busy data is never reused for a different window, because busy times can change between queries. Without the flag, the route is unchanged from the rest of this release: events only, calendar marked not checked. A saved delegated choice remembers whether this was turned on.

Offline: registry and business calls follow HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, and ALL_PROXY. The traced client had been installing its own transport, so httpx ignored those variables and a host that can only leave through a proxy failed discovery with a TLS version error while the plain prerequisite check succeeded. Bracketed IPv6 entries in NO_PROXY, such as [::1], are rewritten to the bare address before any client is built, because httpx reads the colon as a port and raises InvalidURL. The bare address still bypasses the proxy. A caller-supplied transport is unchanged.

Existing businesses and the registry stay compatible: no USP, UCP, or platform profile version changed and no request shape changed. Saved session files keep their format version. The route field takes one more value, a boolean records whether the delegated route can read busy times, and two optional fields hold a pending busy-time request and its one-shot result. Older builds keep fields they do not know when they save. The pending event request still lives in the existing calendar event file.

Hosted replay: Muse (muse.ai), an unpublished checkout of this branch installed editable in its VM, booked the $1 AC Repair at HVAC-Koby on 23/10/26 (booking 6e58be95-05cb-424a-a8fe-a7607582decd, order 4b06764d-6858-4f0b-93cb-84cebec28f46). Link was already signed in. The delegated route was connected with --delegated-can-read-busy: availability asked for busy times, Muse reported 70 intervals from its own Google Calendar, and the returned set went from 130 slots to 118 with calendar_filtered true and calendar_not_checked false. The user picked the soonest remaining time (Fri 23 Oct 2026, 12:15-1:15 PM MST) and said yes. The CLI created a UCP checkout for $1.00, posted the terms URL raw, and returned a Link approval URL. Payment status is paid. flow status is phase CONFIRMED and its user_message is the booked text plus the raw Google Calendar link. The event is on the user's calendar at that instant (shown as 10:15-11:15pm in the viewer's zone) and its description carries the same booking id and order id. runtime doctor is healthy with no findings, and its state directory survived an earlier boot change (runtime_starts 3). Not done: a new conversation after the slot was chosen, and a mid-flow "what's going on?" turn. Muse noticed the Link approval without a further chat message and posted the booked result on its own.
